paper.title: Towards Efficient Online Exploration for Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online RLHF under a multi-armed bandit model (Bradley-Terry preferences, KL-regularized objective)
unmapped: Regret is measured on the KL-regularized objective J(pi, r*) = E_pi[r*] - beta*KL(pi || pi_ref), against the KL-regularized optimal policy pi*, not against the best arm
Rewards r*(a) lie in [0, r_max]; the learner knows r_max, the regularization beta and the reference policy pi_ref
The learner outputs a policy each round and queries a pairwise comparison between actions sampled from pi^(t-1) and pi^(t)
settings.definition_quote: We establish theoretical guarantees for Algorithm~\ref{alg:explore} under the multi-armed bandit setting (i.e., $\mathcal{X}=\varnothing$) with $A=|\mathcal{A}|$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online RLHF bandit, Example 1 / Example 2 (lower bound)
unmapped: Regret is measured on the KL-regularized objective, against the KL-regularized optimal policy pi*
settings.definition_quote: Consider the bandit setting with three actions $\mathcal{A}=\{a_{0},a_{1},a_{2}\}$, where the true rewards are $r^{\star}(a_{0})=1$ and $r^{\star}(a_{1})=r^{\star}(a_{2})=0$.

algorithms.name: Modified exploration scheme sampling a_1~pi^(t), a_2~pi_ref (XPO/SELM-style)

symbols.r_max: upper bound on rewards, r* in [0, r_max]
symbols.Phi_pairs: sum over action pairs with r*(a+)>=r*(a-) of min{ pi_HF(a+)/pi_HF(a-)*alpha_T*r_max, (T*pi_ref(a-)/pi_ref(a+))^(beta/(beta+1)) * alpha_T^(1/(beta+1)) * r_max^(1/(beta+1)) }

tuning: alpha_t > A log T, non-decreasing in t

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Let $\alpha_{t}>A\log T$ be non-decreasing in $t$. There exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that, with probability at least $1-O(T^{-10})$, the cumulative regret of running Algorithm~\ref{alg:explore} for $T$ iterations satisfies \mathcal{R}(T) \leq Cr_{\mathsf{max}}A^{2}\sqrt{T\log T}+C\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{Ar_{\mathsf{max}}\log T}{\alpha_{t}}+CA^{2}\alpha_{T}r_{\mathsf{max}}^{2}+C(r_{\mathsf{max}}+\log T)\sum ... \min\{...\}

results.notes: Failure probability O(T^{-10}). A = number of actions mapped to K. The universal constant C is absorbed into O notation.

symbols.kappa: constant kappa in Assumption 1 (alignment of pi_ref with pi_HF)
symbols.poly_factor: a polynomial in (A, r_max, log T) whose degree does not depend on beta

conditions: Assumption 1: there exist kappa, tau >= 1 such that pi_HF(a+)/pi_HF(a-) >= tau implies pi_ref(a+)/pi_ref(a-) >= 1/kappa
tuning: alpha_t = A log T + t^{1/(beta+2)} (r_max/kappa)^{beta/(beta+2)} (log T/(A(r_max+log T)))^{(beta+1)/(beta+2)}

source.label: prop:regret-1
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption~\ref{assumption:1} holds. Let \alpha_{t}=A\log T+t^{\frac{1}{\beta+2}}(\frac{r_{\max}}{\kappa})^{\frac{\beta}{\beta+2}}(\frac{\log T}{A(r_{\max}+\log T)})^{\frac{\beta+1}{\beta+2}}. Then with probability at least $1-O(T^{-10})$, we have \mathcal{R}(T)\lesssim (\tau + \kappa^\beta T^{\frac{\beta+1}{\beta+2}})\,\mathsf{poly}(A,r_{\max},\log T), where the degree of the polynomial factor does not depend on $\beta$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicitly tau A^3 r_max^2 log^2 T + T^{(beta+1)/(beta+2)} kappa^beta r_max^2 A^3 tau log^2 T. The tuning uses kappa, so the learner needs to know kappa. The printed number is guessed from the shared prop counter (prop:lb=1, prop:2=2).

conditions: specific algorithm: VPO with any alpha>0 and uniform initial policy
Example 1 instance: 3 actions, r*(a0)=1, r*(a1)=r*(a2)=0, uniform pi_ref, pi_cal(a1)=pi_cal(a2)=p<1/4

source.label: prop:lb
source.quote: Consider the setup in Example~\ref{example:1}. Let the initial policy $\pi^{(1)}$ of VPO be the uniform distribution over $\mathcal{A}$. Assume that $r_{\max}/\beta\geq3$. For any $\alpha>0$, with probability at least $4/(9e)$, we have J(\pi^{\star},r^{\star};\pi_{\mathsf{cal}})-J(\pi^{(t)},r^{\star};\pi_{\mathsf{cal}})\geq\frac{1}{2} holds for any $1<t\leq\exp(r_{\max}/\beta)/2$.

results.notes: Per-round suboptimality bound summed over rounds 2..T, giving linear regret over an exponentially long horizon. It holds with constant probability, not 1-delta.

conditions: specific algorithm: modified exploration scheme sampling a_1~pi^(t), a_2~pi_ref, with any alpha>0 and any initial policy
Example 2 instance: 3 actions, r*(a0)=0, r*(a1)=r_max, r*(a2)=r_max-2, pi_ref(a0)=1-2/kappa, kappa>=4

source.label: prop:2
source.quote: Consider the setup in Example~\ref{example:2}. Assume that $\beta\leq 1$ and $\kappa \leq \exp(r_{\max}/\beta)$. For any initial policy $\pi^{(1)}$ and any $\alpha>0$, with probability at least $1/64$, the modified exploration scheme which samples $a_{1}^{t}\sim\pi^{(t)}$ and $a_{2}^{t}\sim\pi_{\mathsf{ref}}$ satisfies J(\pi^{\star},r^{\star};\pi_{\mathsf{ref}})-J(\pi^{(t)},r^{\star};\pi_{\mathsf{ref}})\geq 0.01 for any $1<t\leq \min\{\kappa,\exp(r_{\max})/2\}$.

results.notes: Per-round gap summed over rounds 2..T. Shows that XPO/SELM-style sampling incurs regret linear in kappa. Holds with constant probability.
